sections.title: Seedable Config Architecture + Changelog Versioning (also known as CW Config)

acceptance_tests.definition: Every mutating action through the editor MUST emit exactly ONE `ActivityEvent` (FR-1); double-emits or missing emits are Code-Red audit-integrity bugs.
`ActivityEvent` MUST carry: `EventId`, `UserId`, `ItemId`, `EventType` (typed enum), `Before` snapshot, `After` snapshot, `CreatedAt` (UTC, ISO-8601). Missing any field fails review.

`EventType` MUST be the documented enum (`ItemCreated`, `ItemUpdated`, `ItemMoved`, `ItemDeleted`, `ItemRestored`, `ItemMirrored`, `BoardColumnReordered`, `TemplateApplied`); adding a new type MUST update the enum + this AT — magic-string types are forbidden.
Events MUST persist in a dedicated `activity.db` SQLite (Split-DB pattern, FR-6); sharing user-data DB is forbidden because it slows read paths.
The `ActivityEvent` table MUST follow naming conventions: singular PascalCase, `EventId` PK, indexed on `(UserId, CreatedAt DESC)` for the default feed query.
`Before`/`After` snapshots MUST be stored as JSON columns (NOT serialized as opaque blobs) so future tooling can diff them; opaque blobs fail review.
Default feed page size MUST be 50 (FR-3) — well below the 250-item view limit; uncapped pagination is a Code-Red perf bug.
Feed MUST support filters: `eventType`, `userId`, `dateRange`, `itemSubtree`; filter combination MUST be server-side (client-side filtering on the full table is forbidden).
Per-item history MUST be reachable from the item context menu (FR-4); hiding it under a hidden flag fails review.
"Restore to this state" MUST reapply the inverse of the recorded event (FR-5); silent best-effort restore that drops fields is a Code-Red data-loss bug.

Reversibility MUST match the table: `Created/Updated/Moved/Deleted/Restored/Mirrored/BoardColumnReordered` are fully reversible; `TemplateApplied` is partial — UI MUST show a clear warning before partial restores.
Every restore MUST itself emit an `ActivityEvent` (audit of the audit) so the chain stays inspectable; silent restores are forbidden.
Retention MUST be 30 days by default (FR-7), mirroring trash retention; silent extension beyond 30 d is forbidden — config must be explicit and audited.
Weekly purge job MUST log per-purge counts at INFO and MUST NOT delete events that are referenced by an in-flight restore operation.
A user MUST only see events for items they own OR are shared with (Editor/Admin); cross-user visibility for non-Admins is a Code-Red privacy bug.
Admin "view audit for other users" capability MUST go through the central `hasRole(userId, 'Admin')` helper; bypassing it is forbidden.
Admin pages use the canonical 3-region layout: **header bar** (title + primary action), **filters/actions strip**, **content region**; deviating layouts require a §01 update first.
The actions bar holds AT MOST one Primary button + N Secondary/Ghost buttons; multiple Primary buttons in one bar are forbidden (visual hierarchy violation).
Filter state MUST round-trip through the URL query-string (sharable links, browser history); filters held only in JS state are forbidden.
Active filters render as removable chips with a single "Clear all" affordance; missing the clear-all is a UX bug.
All admin tables use the documented `<Table>` primitive (sticky header, zebra rows, sort affordance, row-action menu); rolling your own `<table>` markup is forbidden.
Tables MUST handle 4 states: loading, empty (zero results), filtered-empty (filter excludes everything), error; missing any state is a UX bug.
Badge variants MUST match the documented semantic mapping (Success=green, Warning=amber, Error=red, Info=blue, Neutral=grey); off-spec colour use is a Code-Red theming bug.
Modals follow the §06 anatomy: header with title + close X, scrollable body, footer with Primary on right + Cancel on left; reversed button order or missing close X fails review.

WP admin notices use the documented `<Notice>` primitive with type ∈ {success, warning, error, info} and dismissibility flag; raw `<div class="notice notice-error">` markup outside the primitive is forbidden.
Persistent (non-dismissible) notices MUST link to a remediation action; standalone "something is broken" notices without a CTA are a UX bug.
Loading skeletons MUST match the final content shape (NOT generic spinners) for surfaces with predictable structure (tables, cards); generic spinners on table loads fail review.
Empty states MUST include: illustration/icon, headline, supporting text, single primary CTA; bare "No results" text is forbidden.
Progress indicators differentiate determinate (known %) vs indeterminate (unknown duration) — using a determinate bar with `value=null` is forbidden.
Pagination controls show: current page, total pages, prev/next, jump-to-first/last (when total > 5 pages); missing jump controls on long pagers fails review.
Misc rules in §11 (focus rings, tab order, keyboard shortcuts on tables/modals) are mandatory accessibility requirements; failing any is a Code-Red a11y bug.

Every "never generate X" rule MUST include: a forbidden code snippet (`❌`), a required code snippet (`✅`), and a one-line rationale; rules missing any of the three fail review because AI cannot self-correct without a positive exemplar.
The rule list MUST cover at minimum: enum invention, type-cast invention, library-API invention, naming-convention invention, and import-path invention; gaps in any category fail review.
Each rule MUST cite an authoritative source file (cross-language or per-language); orphan rules (no citation) fail review because they're un-traceable.
The checklist MUST contain ≤ 50 items, each phrased as a binary check (`[ ] X is …`); open-ended prompts ("consider …") are forbidden because they don't gate output.
Each checklist item MUST link to its enforcing rule (in `01-anti-hallucination-rules.md` OR a cross-language file); checklist items without a deep-link fail review.
The checklist MUST fit in ≤ 200 lines so it can be loaded into AI context windows alongside the task; overlong checklists fail review.
Each catalogued mistake MUST include: a real-world before snippet, a corrected after snippet, AND the rule that was violated; before/after-only entries (no rule citation) fail review.
The catalogue MUST be updated whenever a new repeat-offense pattern is observed in PR review; stale catalogues (no update in > 90 days while issues recur) fail review.
The condensed file MUST fit under 300 lines AND MUST be a true subset of the full master guidelines (NO new rules, NO contradictions); drift between condensed and full is a Code-Red consistency bug.
The condensed file MUST include a `Last synced from master: <date> (UTC+8)` header; missing or stale (> 30 days) sync header fails review.
The quick reference MUST cover all four languages (Go, TypeScript, PHP, Rust) AND MUST agree byte-for-byte with each language's per-language enum spec; divergence is a Code-Red consistency bug.
Each language section MUST cover declaration, naming, usage, AND a validation checklist; missing any of the four sections fails review.

This folder's content MUST be referenced from the project's AI context bootstrap (system prompt, README, or `AI_INSTRUCTIONS.md`); orphan AI-optimization docs not loaded into AI context fail review because they cannot prevent hallucinations they aren't read.

Every rule in this folder MUST be backed by a mechanically checkable enforcement (lint, test, hygiene script, OR review checklist line); rules with no mechanical backing fail review because AI will silently regress them.
Every user has exactly one root `Item`, auto-created on signup, with no parent and undeletable.
`Item.id` is immutable across move, mirror, share, and trash-restore operations.
Every `Item` is a single unified type discriminated by `itemType` (no separate `Project`/`Note`/`Task` tables).
Children are ordered by **fractional-index string keys**, not integer positions.
A view rendering ≥250 items must virtualize or paginate.
Top-level layout has exactly two zones: fixed `NavBar` (top) and scrollable `Page` (below).
Sidebar slides in from the left on Menu click; Esc and outside-click close it.
Back/Forward arrows are disabled (faded) when zoom history is empty/at-end.
Breadcrumb collapses middle segments to "…" when path > 3 segments; hover reveals dropdown.
NavBar Layout Toggle switches the current item between list view and board view.
Field-level conflicts resolve via Last-Write-Wins keyed on server `ServerTs`, with `OwnerId` ASC as tiebreak (per AT-APP-33).
A mutation rejected by the server (validation, 410, etc.) is reverted in the local mirror and surfaced to the user as a non-blocking toast.
Queue persistence survives browser restart; the queue resumes drain from the head on next online event.
Search results are scored into 5 tiers (exact-whole-field=100, prefix=90, substring=80, token=70, fuzzy=60) × field weight.
Within the same tier, results are ordered by `Items.UpdatedAt DESC`.
A query matching both Title (weight 1.0) and Note (weight 0.4) of different items ranks the Title-match higher.
Soft-deleted items (`DeletedAt IS NOT NULL`) are excluded from search results.
Search respects sharing: a user only sees results they have at least `View` permission on (per AT-APP-23).
The Page renders items recursively: `<ItemRow>` contains `<ItemList>` contains `<ItemRow>`. Indentation is visual (margin × depth).
Pressing **Enter** on an item creates a new sibling **after** it; Enter at start with empty content creates a sibling **before**.
**Tab** indents the current item under its previous sibling; **Shift+Tab** outdents. Both must update the fractional index, not re-number siblings.
Drag-and-drop shows the **entire subtree** as the drag preview, not only the dragged row.
Each row exposes a ⋮ button that opens a context menu containing at minimum: Move, Delete, Share, Mirror, Duplicate.
Delete from the menu sends the item to Trash (soft delete) — never hard delete.
Shift+Click extends a contiguous selection range; Cmd/Ctrl+Click toggles individual items.
Bulk operations (move, delete, mirror) act atomically on the selection or roll back on partial failure.
Items in Trash auto-purge **30 days** after deletion.
Restoring a trashed item preserves its original `id`, `parentId`, and child subtree intact.
Roles are stored in a **separate** `user_roles` table — never on the user/profile row.

Authorization checks call a single PHP helper `Auth::hasRole($userId, $role)` (server-side); SQLite queries scope rows by `OwnerId`/share grants in WHERE clauses. No Postgres-style RLS, no `SECURITY DEFINER` — those are not portable to SQLite under WordPress.
Client-side `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` is **never** trusted for admin checks.
A Mirror references the **canonical source** `Item.id` only — never another mirror. Deleting source marks all mirrors broken.
Sharing an item cascades **view** access to all descendants by default.
Today view aggregates items where `itemType = todo` AND `dueDate ≤ today` AND `completedAt IS NULL`, scoped to the current user's accessible items (own + shared-with-edit).
Completing a todo from Today view persists `completedAt = now()` and removes it from the Today list within the same render cycle (no full reload).
Today view honours the `today.includeOverdue` and `today.startOfDay` settings keys; defaults are `true` and `00:00 user-local` respectively.
A Template is a **serialized snapshot** of an item subtree (root + descendants + types + content), stored independently of the source — later edits to the source do **not** mutate the template.

Applying a template inserts a deep copy under the target parent: every node receives a **new** `Item.id`, parent pointers are rewritten, and fractional indices are regenerated to slot at the requested position.

Mirror references inside a template snapshot are **not** preserved as live mirrors on apply — they materialize as plain copies of the referenced content at snapshot time, preventing cross-workspace mirror leaks.
Deleting a template never affects items that were previously instantiated from it.
Conflict resolution is **field-level Last-Writer-Wins** keyed on `(ServerTs, UserId)` per field — never whole-row LWW. Ties on `ServerTs` are broken deterministically by lexicographic `UserId`.

`Mirrors.BrokenAt` follows extended LWW: once set to a non-null timestamp it MAY be moved earlier by a smaller `ServerTs`, but a later non-null write MUST NOT clear it back to `NULL` (broken is sticky against re-link races).
Cascading delete of a source item sets `Mirrors.BrokenAt = source.DeletedAt` for every dependent mirror in the same transaction; no orphan mirrors may remain referencing a trashed/purged source.

Realtime updates use **Server-Sent Events** at `GET /wp-json/workflowy/v1/sync/stream?workspaceId={WorkspaceId}` with `X-WP-Nonce` auth and `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. WebSockets, Pusher, Ably, and long-polling chat protocols are forbidden.

The event vocabulary is a **closed set of 9 names** — `item-updated` (covers create + field changes; new IDs surface as `item-updated` on the new row), `item-deleted`, `item-restored`, `mirror-broken`, `mirror-healed`, `share-granted`, `share-revoked`, `presence` (non-authoritative, droppable), `cursor-overflow` — every event MUST carry a JSON `data:` payload conforming to the schema in §14.5.2. The `:hb` heartbeat comment per AT-APP-41 is **not** an event.
Each SSE message MUST emit `id: {ServerTs}` so clients can resume via the `Last-Event-Id` request header on reconnect.

When SSE is unavailable (corp proxies, offline → online), clients fall back to `GET /wp-json/workflowy/v1/sync/poll?workspaceId={WorkspaceId}&since={LastServerTs}` returning `{ Events, Cursor, HasMore }`. Poll cadence MUST NOT exceed 1 request / 5 s per workspace.
On reconnect the client replays missed events in `ServerTs` order, deduplicates against its local `LastServerTs`, and only then resumes live SSE — no event may be applied twice.
Server emits a heartbeat comment (`: ping\n\n`) every **15 s**; clients treat absence of any frame for **30 s** as a dropped connection and trigger the reconnect+replay algorithm.

If the server cannot replay (cursor older than retention window) it emits a single `cursor-overflow` event; clients MUST respond by issuing a full re-sync of the workspace rather than continuing incremental playback.
Applying a template requires `Edit` or `Admin` on the target parent; `View`-only callers receive **HTTP 403** and no `Items` rows are inserted.
A successful apply makes the new subtree visible to the local client immediately and propagates an SSE `item-updated` (new ID) event to peers within **1 s** under healthy SSE.
Replaying the apply with the same `X-WorkFlowy-Idempotency-Key` within **24 h** returns **HTTP 200** with the original root `ItemId` and inserts no duplicate rows.
If the App-DB INSERT batch fails partway, the entire transaction ROLLBACKs, the client receives **HTTP 500**, and **no SSE event is emitted**.
An inviter without `Admin` on the target item attempting to grant access receives **HTTP 403** and no rows are written to `ItemGrants` or `PendingInvites`.
Sharing with an existing account at role `Edit` returns **HTTP 201**, inserts an `ItemGrants` row with `AcceptedAt = NULL`, and delivers an SSE `share-granted` event to the inviter within **1 s**.
Sharing with a non-existent email returns **HTTP 201** and inserts a `PendingInvites` row in the Root DB with `ExpiresAt = serverNow + 14 days`.

When an invitee clicks the accept link the server returns **HTTP 200**, sets `AcceptedAt = serverNow`, emits SSE `share-granted` (accepted variant) to both parties, and `Auth::hasRole($invitee, 'Edit')` on any descendant of the shared item returns true.
Replayed POST with the same `X-WorkFlowy-Idempotency-Key` returns **HTTP 201** with the original `GrantId` and inserts no duplicate row.
Restoring an item whose parent is also trashed returns **HTTP 422** with `blockingAncestorId` populated and writes nothing to the DB.
Restoring a healthy ancestor first and then a descendant succeeds for both, emitting an SSE `item-restored` event for each.
Restoring an item that has already been **hard-deleted** (purged after the 30-day window) returns **HTTP 410** and the UI removes the row from the Trash list.
A restore racing with a concurrent re-delete carrying a newer `ServerTs` returns **HTTP 409**; the item stays trashed and the field-level LWW rule (AT-APP-33) is respected.
Restoring an item heals its broken mirrors by clearing `Mirrors.BrokenAt` via LWW (subject to AT-APP-34 stickiness) and emits an SSE `mirror-healed` event.
A stale restore racing with the reaper's hard-delete loses LWW: the reaper's newer `ServerTs` wins and the broken-mirror state is preserved.
Mirroring item X under parent P creates a peer-group `G` and inserts P-scoped peer P₂ such that `MirrorPeerGroupMembers` contains both X and P₂ with the same `PeerGroupId`.
Editing the title of any peer in `G` updates `Items.Title` of the canonical content row, and an SSE `item-updated` event fans out to all peers within **1 s**.
`ParentId`, `SortOrder`, and `Permissions` are stored per peer (not per group) and are independent across peers.
Detaching peer P₁ removes it from `MirrorPeerGroupMembers`; if the group's surviving member count drops to **1**, the group is auto-dissolved (group row deleted, last member's PeerGroupId nulled).
Cycle-prevention algorithm rejects a mirror operation that would create a peer of an ancestor of itself, returning **HTTP 409**.
Soft-deleting one peer does NOT delete other peers; the group survives at size ≥2.
Hard-deleting (reaper) a peer that drops the group to size 1 triggers auto-dissolve via DB trigger within the same transaction.
LWW conflicts on shared content fields use server `ServerTs` with `OwnerId` ASC tiebreak.
Mirror peer-group migration script v1→v2 converts every legacy `Mirrors(SourceId, MirrorId)` pair into a peer-group with both rows as members; idempotent re-runs are no-ops.
The legacy `Mirrors` table is read-only after v2 migration; writes return **HTTP 410**.
Dashboard view renders **only** direct children of the zoomed item (depth = 1); grandchildren are not displayed.
Each card displays the child's title and completion checkbox; both are inline-editable.
Toggling between List, Board, and Dashboard never mutates the tree structure — only `Items.ItemType` of the parent changes.
Editing a card title persists to `Items.Title` of the underlying child within **150 ms** debounce.
Toggling a card's checkbox persists to `Items.CompletedAt` of the underlying child.
Clicking into a card zooms to that child; back navigation returns to the dashboard with state preserved.
A dashboard with ≥250 direct children virtualizes per AT-APP-05.
Switching back to List view restores the original child ordering by `SortOrder`.
`Permissions` rows are keyed by `ItemId`, never by `PeerGroupId`. Sharing peer P₁ inserts a Permissions row only for P₁'s `ItemId`.
Recipient of a shared peer P₁ sees content edits from peer P₂ propagated to P₁ within **1 s** via peer-group sync.
Recipient editing P₁'s `ParentId` or `SortOrder` does NOT change P₂'s `ParentId` or `SortOrder`.
Revoking access to peer P₁ does NOT revoke access to peer Pₖ that the same user was independently granted.
When sharing a subtree R that contains peer P₁, the recipient cannot navigate to peer P₂ that lives outside R, even though P₁'s content updates reflect P₂'s edits.
Reaper runs daily at 03:00 UTC and hard-deletes every `Items` row where `DeletedAt < now() - INTERVAL '30 days'`, in batches of 1,000.
Items with `DeletedAt = now() - 29d` survive a reaper pass and remain restorable.
Hard-deleting an item cascades to its children, mirror peer-group memberships, and permissions via FK `ON DELETE CASCADE`.
If a reap drops a peer-group to size 1, the group auto-dissolves in the same transaction (per AT-APP-61/64).
Each reaper run inserts one row into `ReaperRuns(Id, RanAt, RowsDeleted, DurationMs)`.
Triggering zoom while N>1 items are selected opens an ephemeral virtual scope with synthetic parent `virtual:<sessionId>` titled "N items".
Edits inside the virtual scope persist to the **real** `Items` rows (titles, completion).
Pressing `Esc` or breadcrumb-up exits the virtual scope and restores the original selection in the real tree.
If the virtual-scope membership drops to 1 (item deleted), the scope auto-collapses to a normal zoom on the surviving item.
Drag operations are locked to within-scope reordering; drag out-of-scope is rejected with a no-drop cursor.
Page refresh discards the virtual scope (ephemeral, client-only state); user lands on the last persisted scope.
Instantiating template T under parent P creates N new `Items` rows with **fresh UUIDs**; no `TemplateId` FK is set.
Editing T's `PayloadJson` does NOT modify any previously instantiated `Items` rows.
Editing an instantiated `Items` row does NOT modify T's `PayloadJson`.
Mirror peer-groups inside T's payload collapse to plain items on instantiation (no `MirrorPeerGroupMembers` rows created from a template apply).
The `OwnerId` of every instantiated row equals `auth.uid()` of the instantiating user, regardless of T's author.
The full account tree is mirrored locally (IndexedDB) so all CRUD operations work while offline.
Local mutations are appended to a FIFO queue and optimistically applied to the local mirror; UI never blocks on network.
On reconnect, the queue is drained in **strict insertion order**; the server timestamps each accepted mutation and broadcasts via SSE.
**I-1 Round-Trip**: every `*AppError` survives `json.Marshal` → `json.Unmarshal` with code, message, details, values, diagnostics, stack, and cause-message preserved.
**I-2 No raw `error` in structs**: any struct field holding an error MUST be typed `*AppError`, never the bare `error` interface.
**I-3 Stack always present**: every constructor (`New`, `Wrap`, `NewType`, `WrapType`, `FailNew`, `FailWrap`, `FailSlice*`, `FailMap*`) attaches a non-empty `StackTrace` at creation.
**I-4 Zero raw error returns**: every exported service method returns `*AppError`, `Result[T]`, `ResultSlice[T]`, or `ResultMap[K,V]` — never bare `error`.
`StackFrame` has exactly the fields `Function string`, `File string`, `Line int` and a `String()` formatter producing `"function\n      file:line"`.
`StackTrace.Frames` is capped at **18 frames** by default; `CaptureStackN` allows custom depth.
Runtime-frame filtering uses `strings.HasPrefix(fn, "runtime.")` (not `Contains`) to avoid false positives on domain functions.
Re-wrapping an `*AppError` preserves the original trace in `PreviousTrace`; `HasPrevious()` returns `true` after one re-wrap.
Skip values match the canonical table: `New`→2, `Wrap`/`FailWrap`/`FailSliceWrap`/`FailMapWrap`→3, `FailNew`/`FailSliceNew`/`FailMapNew`→3 (via `NewWithSkip(…,1)`).
Every error code is a string constant in `codes.go` (or its `apperrtype` registry); raw string literals like `"E2010"` are forbidden in calling code once an `apperrtype` variant exists.
Code ranges follow the documented domain map (E1xxx config … E14xxx crypto); new codes must occupy the correct range.
`apperrtype.Variation` is a single `uint16` enum with `NoError=0`, ascending values, and a sentinel `MaxError`; all variants live in `types/apperrtype/variation.go`.
`variantRegistry` maps every `Variation` → `VariantStructure{Name, Code, Message, Variant}` and `Variation` implements the `ErrorType` interface (`Code()`, `Message()`, `Name()`).
`apperror.NewType(v)` and `apperror.WrapType(v, …)` are the canonical builders for any `apperrtype.Variation`; raw `New("Exxxx", "msg")` is reserved for prototyping only.
All `apperror` package files target ≤300 lines; 301–400 lines requires the header comment `// NOTE: Needs refactor — exceeds 300-line target`; >400 lines is forbidden.

`AppError` is declared as a single concrete struct (not an interface); fields match the §01 spec exactly — `Variation`, `Code`, `Message`, `Cause`, `StackTrace`, `Diagnostics`, `Values`, plus the diagnostic option blocks listed in the parent reference.
All `AppError` fields are unexported OR exported per the spec's stated access table; field-level mutation outside the package is forbidden — callers use the fluent setters.
The basic constructor set is exactly **`New`, `Wrap`, `NewType`, `WrapType`, `WrapTypeMsg`** — no other top-level constructor is exported.
`Wrap*` constructors preserve the original error in `Cause` and append (do not replace) the existing stack trace; the resulting depth respects the apperror reference budget (18 frames).
The convenience set is exactly **`PathError`, `UrlError`, `SlugError`, `SiteError`, `EndpointError`** — each pre-fills the matching diagnostic block before applying user options.
**Key Rule (parent §00)** — when a diagnostic field is relevant, the convenience constructor MUST be used; manual `.WithXxx()` chaining for the same diagnostic is a lint failure.
`Merge` aggregates a slice of `*AppError` into a single batch error and de-duplicates identical `(Code, Variation)` pairs; `MergeWithCode` overrides the resulting top-level code.
`Merge` returns `nil` when the input slice is empty or contains only nils; this short-circuit is part of the contract and is covered by a unit test.

`Error()` returns a single-line summary, `String()` returns a multi-line developer view, `FullString()` includes the full stack + diagnostics, and `ToClipboard()` produces the canonical copy-to-paste format documented in §05.
All display methods are deterministic for the same input (timestamps formatted in UTC, fields in fixed order); golden-file tests guard regression.

Query methods (`Values`, `IsType`, `IsCode`, `Has*`) are read-only; fluent setters (`WithPath`, `WithUrl`, `WithSlug`, `WithSite`, `WithEndpoint`, …) return the receiver for chaining and never mutate a shared receiver in place.
Flow-control helpers (`MustReturn`, `OrPanic`, `OrLogAndContinue` — names per §06) are documented with their failure mode and an explicit test verifying the panic / log path.
`Variation` is declared as `type Variation uint16` — never `byte`, `int`, or string-backed; this is a breaking-change marker tracked at the package level.
All variants are organized into the documented domain ranges **E1xxx–E18xxx** (18 ranges); a variant outside its declared range fails the registry-bounds check.
`VariantStructure` carries exactly `Name`, `Code`, `Message` (typed strings); no additional fields are added without a spec bump.
`ErrorType` interface exposes `Variation()`, `Code()`, `Message()`, `Name()`; every variant satisfies the interface implicitly via `Variation` methods.

`Variation` type has `String()`, `Code()`, `Message()`, `Name()`, `IsValid()`, and `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` methods; JSON serialization uses the `Code` string (e.g., `"E2010"`), NOT the numeric value.
`variantRegistry` is a single package-level `map[Variation]VariantStructure`; the package exposes only read methods on `Variation`, never the map directly.
`minValue` / `maxValue` consts bound the legal range; `IsValid()` returns `false` for any value outside `[minValue, maxValue]` OR not present in the registry.
A package-init test verifies that every declared variant constant is present in the registry and falls inside its documented domain range.
`StringToVariantMap` and `CodeToVariantMap` are derived from the registry at init; both are bijections (every `Variation` appears in exactly one entry of each map).
Reverse lookup of an unknown name/code returns the zero value AND a `false` ok-bool; callers MUST check the bool before use.
Display format strings live in `format_consts.go` (per §00 package layout); changing a format string is a spec change.

Adding a new variant requires: (a) declaring the constant in the correct domain range, (b) registering its `VariantStructure`, (c) adding a registry test, (d) bumping the package version per the spec's version policy.
The v1.x → v2.0 migration (per-domain `byte` → unified `uint16` `Variation`) is documented with a before/after example and a one-time codemod note; legacy `byte` enums are removed, not aliased.

When `return` (or `throw`) is preceded by **at least one other statement** in the same block, exactly **one** blank line MUST appear between them.
When `return`/`throw` is the **only** statement in the block (e.g., guard clause body), NO blank line is required (and adding one is a style violation).
Multiple consecutive blank lines are forbidden; the rule produces **exactly one** blank line, not two.
A closing `}` followed by **more code** in the same scope MUST be followed by exactly one blank line before that next statement.
The rule does NOT apply when the next token is `else`, `else if`, `catch`, `finally`, or another chainable continuation; those follow on the same line.
The rule does NOT apply at the end of a parent block (closing `}` immediately followed by another closing `}`).
The rule applies uniformly to function bodies, control-structure blocks, and inline anonymous functions/closures.
A control structure (`if`/`for`/`while`/`switch`/`do`) preceded by **another statement** MUST have exactly one blank line before it.
The rule does NOT apply when the control structure is the **first statement** in its block (no preceding statement).
The rule applies to nested-but-not-stacked control structures: a `for` loop directly after another statement gets the blank line, even when both are inside a parent block.

Boolean variables, fields, and methods use a **positive `is`/`has`/`can`/`should`** prefix; `not`, `disable`, `block`, `prevent` prefixes are forbidden.
The prefix MUST match the underlying truth value — `isReady` returns `true` when ready, NEVER `true` when "not ready"; inverted-meaning names fail review.
Pluralized boolean fields (`areReady`) are forbidden; an array semantic uses `hasAny<X>()` or `count` instead of a plural boolean.
The canonical guard set is `isDefined(x)`, `isDefinedAndValid(x)`, `isEmpty(x)` (and their language-specific equivalents); `if (!x)` and bare truthiness checks in business logic are forbidden.
Compound conditions (≥3 sub-expressions OR mixed AND/OR) MUST be extracted into a **positively-named local boolean** before the `if` statement.
Negation in compound conditions (`!isX && isY`) is forbidden — assign the negation to a positive-named local first (e.g., `isXAbsent := !isX; if isXAbsent && isY`).
**Boolean flag parameters** are forbidden — split into two named methods (`processSync()` / `processAsync()`) or accept a typed enum/options object.
A function returning `bool` does NOT take a `bool` parameter that controls its return polarity (no `getStatus(invert: true)` patterns).
Ternary `cond ? true : false` (or its negation) is forbidden — return `cond` (or `!cond`) directly.
The quick-reference table in §04 lists the canonical "DO / DON'T" for every rule above; each row links back to the rule file.

Documented exemptions (e.g., third-party API boundaries that require `disabled: true`, framework lifecycle props with negative names) are listed by name in §05; undocumented use of a forbidden pattern fails review.

At an external API boundary, the negative form is converted to a positive form **inside** the adapter — e.g., `disabled: true` from props becomes `isDisabled: true` then `isEnabled := !isDisabled` for internal use.

The system implements a strict 3-tier error-handling architecture: **Tier 1 = Delegated server (PHP / 3rd-party)**, **Tier 2 = Go backend**, **Tier 3 = React frontend** — every error crosses tiers via the universal envelope only.
The 3-hop request chain (React → Go → Delegated) is documented with a flow diagram and every hop captures structured diagnostics (request, response, stack, code).
Delegated servers wrap every endpoint in a `safe_execute()` boundary that converts uncaught exceptions into the universal envelope with a registered error code.
Delegated servers write a per-request `stacktrace.txt` via `FileLogger` to a session-scoped directory; the path is returned in the envelope's `Data.LogPath` for cross-tier diagnostics.
The Go backend uses `apperror.New` / `apperror.Wrap` / `apperror.NewType` for every error — bare `error` returns are forbidden across exported service methods.

When proxying to a delegated server, Go injects a `DelegatedRequestServer` block into the `*AppError` containing the upstream URL, method, status, request body summary, response body summary, and upstream stack (if returned).
The Go backend's HTTP layer always serializes `*AppError` to the universal envelope; HTTP status mirrors the `apperror` policy mapping (4xx for client errors, 5xx for server errors).

Every Go enum MUST live in its own package `pkg/enums/<name>type/` and follow the documented file layout (`variant.go`, `parser.go`, `validator.go`); ad-hoc `const ( … iota )` blocks scattered in business packages are forbidden.
Enum types MUST be `type Foo string` (NOT `type Foo int` / `iota`); string-backed enums are mandatory for wire-format stability.
Each enum MUST expose `String()`, `IsValid()`, and `Parse(raw string)` methods; missing any of the three is a Code-Red enforcement bug.
Boolean variables / functions MUST start with `Is`/`Has`/`Should`/`Can`/`Will`; non-prefixed booleans fail lint.
Boolean function parameters MUST be replaced with split methods OR a typed enum (NOT `func DoThing(force bool)`); boolean flag params are forbidden.
`defer` MUST be placed immediately after the resource is acquired (`f, err := os.Open(…); if err != nil { … }; defer f.Close()`); deferring later is a Code-Red leak bug.
`defer` in a loop MUST be wrapped in a function (or refactored) — un-wrapped loop defers are a Code-Red leak bug because they accumulate until function exit.

`string([]byte)` and `[]byte(string)` conversions MUST be avoided in hot paths; use `unsafe.String` / `unsafe.Slice` ONLY behind a documented helper with a benchmark — bare unsafe casts are forbidden.
Slice growth in hot paths MUST pre-allocate via `make([]T, 0, cap)`; un-capped `append` in a known-length loop is a perf bug.
Every coding-rule violation MUST be tagged with one of the documented severities (`Code-Red` / `Code-Orange` / `Code-Yellow` / `Code-Green`); un-severitied violations fail review.
`Code-Red` issues MUST block merge in CI; downgrading via inline comments requires a tracking ID and PR review.

All filesystem path manipulation MUST go through the `pathutil` package (NOT `path/filepath` directly in business code); raw `filepath.Join` outside `pathutil` is forbidden because it bypasses traversal protection.
All file I/O MUST go through the `fileutil` package, which enforces atomic-write semantics (temp + rename); raw `os.WriteFile` in business code is forbidden because crash-mid-write corrupts data.
The standards-reference subfolder MUST be the SSOT for Go-specific rules; any rule duplicated outside this folder MUST link back here — drift is a Code-Red consistency bug.
Files ≤ 300 lines (hard max 400), functions ≤ **15 logical lines**, parameters ≤ **3**; longer functions/files MUST be extracted/split.
**Nested `if` is forbidden** — use early-return guards or extracted helpers; documented exemptions only.
File names use `snake_case.go` and group by domain (not by layer); test files MUST be `_test.go` siblings of the unit they test.
`interface{}` / `any` are forbidden in business logic; type switches require an explicit `default` branch that returns a typed error.
Errors are constructed via the `apperror` package with stack trace; raw `errors.New` / `fmt.Errorf` in business code is forbidden.
Functions return at most ONE result value plus error (`(T, error)` or `Result[T]`); 3+ return values fail review unless documented as a constructor exception.
Errors are NEVER swallowed — every `if err != nil` branch logs OR returns OR wraps; empty branches and `_ = err` are forbidden.
Database tables/columns/keys use **PascalCase**; primary keys are `{TableName}Id`.
All DB calls go through the `dbutil` wrapper (parameterized, instrumented); raw `db.Exec` / `db.Query` in handlers is forbidden.
Structs separate domain (immutable value), DTO (transport), and persistence (DB row) — single struct serving all three roles is forbidden.
Booleans use positive `Is`/`Has`/`Can`/`Should` prefixes; negative prefixes are forbidden; guards are `isDefined`/`isEmpty` style.
Enums use typed `const` blocks with a base type alias (e.g., `type Status uint8`); raw string/int literals representing enum values are forbidden.
Independent goroutines use `errgroup` (or documented equivalent) — bare `go func()` without recover OR error reporting is forbidden in production code.
Forbidden patterns listed in §06 (e.g., naked `panic`, mutable globals, `init()` with side effects) MUST NOT appear in the codebase; each forbidden item names the safe replacement.

Two log tiers exist: **operational log** (always-on, INFO+) and **debug log** (gated by debug-mode constant); merging them into one tier is forbidden.
Debug mode is toggled by a single constant (e.g., `RISEUP_DEBUG`) defined in `wp-config.php`; runtime toggling via DB is forbidden.
The file logger writes to `wp-content/uploads/<plugin>/logs/<YYYY-MM-DD>.log`; logging to `wp-content/debug.log` directly is forbidden.
Every log entry uses the canonical 5-field format: `[timestamp] [level] [requestId] [source] message`; printf-style entries that skip fields fail review.
`requestId` is generated once per HTTP request (UUIDv4 or 16-hex) and propagated through the request lifecycle; missing `requestId` on any entry is a bug.
Stacktraces are written to a sibling `<YYYY-MM-DD>.stacktrace.log` (NOT inlined into the operational log); inlining stacktraces in operational entries is forbidden.
Log rotation triggers on size (default 10 MiB) AND age (default 14 days); both thresholds are configurable via the seedable-config layer.
The transport format for stacktraces sent to the client uses the documented JSON envelope in §10 (NOT the on-disk format).
Identical log entries within a configured window (default 60 s) are deduplicated with a `(seen N times)` suffix; the dedup key is `(level, source, message)` (NOT including timestamp).
Bare `catch (\Throwable)` that returns `null`/`false` without logging is **Code Red**; every catch logs at ERROR level with a stacktrace.
`SafeExecute::run(callable, $context)` is the only sanctioned wrapper for "log-and-return-default" semantics; ad-hoc try/catch+log helpers in business code are forbidden.
`SafeExecute` MUST attach `$context` to the log entry (operation name, key inputs); calls that pass no context fail review.
API error responses use `WP_Error` wrapped by `Helpers\Responses::error($code, $message, $statusCode)`; `wp_send_json_error()` with raw arrays is forbidden.
The `ErrorLogHelper` class is the only sanctioned entry to file-logging from production code; `error_log()`, `var_dump()`, `echo` for debugging are forbidden.
Date helpers use `wp_date()` (timezone-aware) — `date()` (server-tz) is forbidden in log entries.

A shutdown handler captures fatal errors via `error_get_last()` and writes them to the operational log + stacktrace file; absence of the shutdown handler is a Code-Red bug. End-to-end flow §15 is the integration SSOT.
Database tables, columns, and keys use **PascalCase**; primary keys are `{TableName}Id` with `INTEGER AUTOINCREMENT` (SQLite) or matching dialect equivalent.
All SQL is parameterized — string concatenation into SQL is forbidden; joins use views, not inline JOIN statements in business code.
Booleans use positive `is`/`has`/`can`/`should` prefixes; negative prefixes (`not`, `disable`, `block`, `prevent`) are forbidden.
Enums replace magic strings/numbers in business logic; raw string literals representing a finite set are a review failure.
Functions ≤ **15 logical lines**, files ≤ 300 (hard max 400), parameters ≤ **3**; nested `if` is forbidden.
**Errors are never swallowed** (Code Red): every catch/recover MUST log + return OR re-throw with context; empty catches fail review.
Go errors use the `apperror` package with stack trace; raw `errors.New` / `fmt.Errorf` in business code is forbidden.
`any` (TS), `interface{}`/`any` (Go), and untyped arrays/maps are forbidden in business logic; type assertions require a runtime guard.
Discriminated unions use **named** interfaces — inline variant types in function signatures are forbidden.
Magic numbers are forbidden — every numeric literal in business logic MUST come from a named constant or enum (exemptions: 0, 1, -1 in arithmetic).
Code is organized by domain (feature folder), not by technical layer (no top-level `controllers/`, `services/`, `repositories/` for the whole app).
Independent async work uses `Promise.all` (TS) / goroutines + errgroup (Go) — sequential awaits over independent calls fail review.
Caches require a TTL; unbounded caches are forbidden. Cache invalidation on mutation is mandatory; never cache an error response as a success.

Every example block MUST be copy-paste runnable on a clean PowerShell 7+ session (no implicit `cd`, no undocumented prerequisites); broken examples are a Code-Red docs bug.
Each example MUST show the expected exit code (0 / non-zero) so users know what success looks like; ambiguous examples fail review.
Every helper function MUST document `Synopsis`, `Parameters`, `Returns`, and `Example` using PowerShell comment-based help (`<# .SYNOPSIS … #>`); missing comment-help blocks fail lint.
Function names MUST follow `Verb-Noun` PowerShell convention with an approved verb (`Get-Verb`); custom verbs are forbidden.
Each pipeline step MUST log a `▶ Step N/Total: <name>` header so users can track progress; silent steps are forbidden.
A step failure MUST short-circuit the pipeline AND emit a typed exit code (NOT a generic `1`); silent continue-on-error is a Code-Red reliability bug.
Final summary MUST print elapsed time per step AND total elapsed time; missing the breakdown fails review.
Exit codes MUST be drawn from a documented enum (`ExitCode.Success = 0`, `ExitCode.ConfigError = 2`, `ExitCode.PipelineFailure = 3`, etc.); ad-hoc numeric exits are forbidden.
`pnpm store` invocations MUST go through a wrapper that pins the pnpm major version; calling `pnpm` directly with no version check is forbidden because lockfile drift breaks reproducibility.
Cache-clear operations MUST require `-Force` to prevent accidental wipes; a missing confirmation is a Code-Red destructive-action bug.
`wpPlugins` config blocks MUST validate against a JSON schema before use; invalid configs MUST fail fast with a pointer to the offending field — silent skip is forbidden.
Plugin upload destinations MUST be parameterized via the config — hardcoded WordPress paths in `upload-plugin-*.ps1` are forbidden because they prevent multi-environment use.
The version-detection flow in §01 decides **merge vs skip** by comparing `config.seed.json.version` against `ConfigMeta.version` in the DB; no other input is consulted.
Merge is **additive**: new keys are inserted, existing user-overridden values are preserved (NEVER overwritten); the merge algorithm in §01 is the SSOT.
The pattern requires exactly three artifacts: `config.seed.json`, `config.schema.json`, `CHANGELOG.md`; missing any of the three fails project bootstrap.
`config.seed.json` MUST validate against `config.schema.json` at build time (CI gate); a schema-invalid seed fails CI.
`CHANGELOG.md` follows the documented Keep-a-Changelog-style format; missing entries for the current version block release.
The schema defines exactly three tables: `ConfigMeta`, `Setting`, `SettingHistory` — all in **PascalCase** with `{TableName}Id` primary keys.
`SettingHistory` MUST capture every change to `Setting` (insert, update, delete) with `(settingKey, oldValue, newValue, changedAt, changedBy)`; missing audit rows is a Code-Red bug.
`SettingValue` is a **typed union** (string, number, boolean, JSON-object); `interface{}` / `any` containers are forbidden.
Each setting in `config.seed.json` declares its `valueType` matching one of the union variants; runtime type mismatch triggers a typed `apperror`.
All config access goes through `ConfigService`; direct queries against the `Setting` table from handlers/services are forbidden.
`ConfigService.SeedWithVersionCheck()` is idempotent — running it twice on the same seed version performs zero writes.
Bump rules: **major** = removed keys or breaking type change; **minor** = new keys; **patch** = description/help-text only. Releasing a bump that violates these rules fails review.
The version badge (showing current `ConfigMeta.version`) AND the new-settings highlight (rendered for keys added in the last bump) are mandatory React components when the project ships a settings UI.
Theme settings use the documented CSS-variable contract (light + dark) and integrate with the project theme provider; raw hex/rgb values in theme settings are forbidden.

The **no-hardcoded-arrays policy** forbids enumerated value sets (e.g., a list of supported providers) being hardcoded in business code — they MUST live in `config.seed.json` and be loaded via `ConfigService`.
The updater MUST check the configured manifest URL, compare the remote version against the running binary version (semver), and only proceed when the remote is strictly greater.
Deploy-path resolution MUST be deterministic and never rely on the current working directory; symlinks and renamed binaries are handled explicitly per `02-deploy-path-resolution.md`.
Rename-first deploy: the new binary is downloaded next to the live binary, verified, then renamed-into-place atomically; the old binary is preserved for rollback.
Hand-off from the old process to the new process re-execs cleanly without leaking sockets, file descriptors, or partial writes.
Cleanup removes the prior binary only after the new binary has booted successfully past a documented healthcheck; failed boot triggers rollback.
Every downloaded asset is verified against a SHA-256 checksum from a signed manifest before any rename-into-place; verification failure aborts the update — Code Red on bypass.
The release manifest is the SSOT for `Version`, `Channel`, `Url`, `Sha256`, `MinPreviousVersion`; missing or extra keys MUST be rejected.

Release versioning rules (auto-bump, tagging, changelog, branch strategy) are owned by [`09-release-versioning/`](./09-release-versioning/00-overview.md); see its rollup [`AT-RELEASEVERSIONING-NN`](./09-release-versioning/97-acceptance-criteria.md).
Cross-compilation matrix matches the documented platform list; missing a platform is a release-blocking defect.
The release pipeline produces install scripts that are idempotent (re-running on an up-to-date system MUST be a no-op) and the updater binary is statically linked or ships its runtime.
Network requirements are documented (allow-list of hosts, ports, fallback CDNs) so corp environments can pre-flight; the updater MUST NOT contact undocumented hosts.
The `update` command workflow has a documented dry-run mode that performs all checks short of rename-into-place.

Every HTTP request is assigned a unique **session ID** at the edge (middleware), echoed in `Attributes.SessionId` of the universal envelope, and propagated across the 3-hop chain (React → Go → Delegated).
The session capture is **complete** — request line, headers (redacted), body summary (truncated), response status, response body summary, and timing — all 6 fields MUST be present per request.
When the Go backend proxies a request, a **`DelegatedRequestInfo`** sub-record is captured with the upstream URL, method, status, body summaries, and any upstream stack returned in the envelope.

`RequestSession` carries `SessionId`, `StartedAt`, `FinishedAt`, `RequestSummary`, `ResponseSummary`, `DelegatedRequests []DelegatedRequestInfo`, `Errors []ErrorRef`; field names are stable for cross-tier consumers.
Session-error linkage is bidirectional: the session lists `ErrorRef`s, and every emitted `*AppError` carries the originating `SessionId` in its diagnostic block.
The system exposes **8 REST endpoints** documented in §04 (list, get, search, purge, export, etc.); endpoint signatures match the documented method + path + envelope shape exactly.
Every endpoint returns the universal envelope; endpoints that paginate include `Attributes.Page`, `Attributes.PageSize`, `Attributes.TotalCount`.

All knobs (storage path, max body size, retention days, redaction rules, sample rate) are exposed via the documented config schema AND the matching environment variables; CLI flags override env, env overrides config file.

**Redaction** rules in §06 are applied BEFORE persistence — Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, password-like body keys, and configured custom keys are replaced with `"<redacted>"`; raw values must never reach disk.
**Truncation** caps body summaries at the documented byte budget (per §06); truncated payloads carry an explicit `truncated: true` marker.
**Retention** runs on a documented schedule and deletes sessions older than the configured `RetentionDays`; deletion is logged.
The canonical `error.log` format documented in §07 is the SOLE textual error format; deviations (different field order, missing field) fail a golden-file test.
The implementation file map in §07 lists every concrete artifact required (middleware, store, redactor, retention worker, REST handlers); the hygiene cross-ref check resolves every name.

The test plan in §08 covers at minimum: full 3-hop happy path, redaction correctness, truncation correctness, retention deletion, and pagination edge cases; the metrics list (sessions/sec, redaction count, retention deletes) is exported on the metrics endpoint.

Anti-patterns listed in §13 (god-options-row, raw `update_option` outside the registry, hidden fields used as state, JS-driven validation as the only validation tier) MUST NOT appear in the codebase.

All enums MUST use TypeScript `enum` syntax with PascalCase values AND a `Type` suffix on the enum name (e.g., `enum HttpMethodType { Get = 'Get' }`); string-union types as a substitute are forbidden.
Each enum MUST live in its own `src/lib/enums/<name>.ts` file (one enum per file); colocating multiple enums in a single file is forbidden because it harms grep-ability.
Enum values MUST be string literals matching the enum-key name (`Foo = 'Foo'`); numeric enums and divergent value/key are forbidden because they break wire-format stability.
Each enum file MUST export the enum AND a typed parser (`parseHttpMethodType(raw: string): HttpMethodType`); inline `as` casts in callers are forbidden.
The codebase MUST contain ZERO `any` annotations; the type-safety remediation plan MUST track every legacy occurrence with a removal target date — open items past target fail review.
`unknown` MUST be confined to boundary parsing (Zod inputs, `JSON.parse` results); business code MUST narrow `unknown` to a typed shape via a schema before use — propagating `unknown` is forbidden.
`Record<string, unknown>` MUST NOT appear in public APIs — generic-first signatures (`<T extends Record<string, …>>`) are mandatory.
ESLint enforcement MUST cover every TS rule listed in `11-eslint-enforcement.md`; missing rule wiring fails CI — drift between docs and `.eslintrc` is a Code-Red enforcement bug.
Every standards-reference rule MUST cite its enforcement mechanism (compile / lint / runtime / test); rules without an enforcement column fail review because they're un-auditable.
Every reference rule MUST include a positive (`✅`) AND negative (`❌`) code example; rule docs without both fail review.
`await` MUST be paired with explicit `try/catch` OR a dedicated `safeAwait` helper; bare `await` in business code that propagates rejection is a Code-Red error-handling bug.
`Promise.all` MUST be used for independent parallel ops; sequential `await` chains where parallel is possible fail review (perf bug).
Floating promises (un-awaited, no `.catch`) are forbidden; `no-floating-promises` ESLint rule MUST be set to `error`.
Action / message / state shapes MUST use discriminated unions with a `kind` (or `type`) string-literal tag; bag-of-optionals shapes are forbidden because they break exhaustiveness checks.
Every union switch MUST have an exhaustiveness `assertNever(x)` default arm; missing the default is a Code-Red maintainability bug because new variants silently slip through.
Discriminated union variants MUST NOT share the same `kind` value; collisions are a Code-Red type-safety bug.
**Generics first** — every reusable function, hook, and component that operates on a value type accepts a generic parameter; concrete-typed copies for each shape are forbidden.
**Zero `any`** — `any` and untyped `Function`/`Object` are banned; `unknown` is the only acceptable escape hatch and must be narrowed before use.
**No magic strings/numbers** — every literal that is reused or carries domain meaning lives in a `const`, enum, or `as const` map; raw literals in business logic are flagged.
**catch blocks** type the caught value as `unknown` (or rely on TS `useUnknownInCatchVariables`) and use a typed narrowing helper (`isAppError`, `isError`) before access.
**React Query** keys are typed arrays `[domain, id, …filters]` and the query/mutation generics declare both data and error shapes (`useQuery<TData, TError>`).
**Prop drilling** beyond 2 levels is replaced with a typed React Context or Zustand slice; raw `any` props are not allowed to pass through intermediate components.
**Function size** ≤ 15 logical lines (excluding signature, braces, blank lines, comments).
**Zero nested `if`** — nested `if` statements are forbidden; use early-return guard clauses, `switch`, or extracted helpers.

**Enforcement** — `tsconfig.json` enables `strict`, `noImplicitAny`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `useUnknownInCatchVariables`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`; ESLint enables `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and `no-magic-numbers`.
**Positive guards** — `isDefined(x)`, `isDefinedAndValid(x)`, `isEmpty(x)` are the canonical guards; `if (!x)` and `if (x == null)` are forbidden in business logic.
**Discriminated unions** are declared with named interfaces and an enum-typed discriminator field; inline shape literals inside a union are not allowed.
**Generics reference table** in `09-generics-reference.md` is the SSOT for "when to use what generic"; new generic helpers must be added to this table before use.
**Frontend enum inventory** — every TS enum/literal-union listed in `10-enum-inventory.md` has Go parity (case names + values); drift is caught by `scripts/spec-hygiene/15-check-enums-in-sync.mjs`.
**Response envelope** — every fetch/axios call validates the response against the universal envelope schema (`Success`, `Code`, `Message`, `Data`) before returning to the caller.

Every package/module that defines shared types has a dedicated **`types/`** subfolder (Go: `internal/<domain>/types/`, TS: `src/<domain>/types/`, PHP: `includes/<Domain>/Types/`); types declared inline in service/handler files fail review.
Folder structure is **flat or 1-level deep**; nesting beyond `types/<sub>/<file>` is forbidden — split into a sibling `types/` instead.
The `types/` folder MUST NOT import from `services/`, `handlers/`, or `repositories/`; reverse dependency arrow only (types is the lowest layer).
**One definition per file** — each `.go`/`.ts`/`.php` file in `types/` defines exactly ONE primary type (plus its directly-related helper aliases); files with multiple unrelated structs fail review.
Repeated generic instantiations (e.g., `Result[User]` used 5+ times) MUST be promoted to a named type alias (`type UserResult = Result[User]`); inline repetition is forbidden.
Enums replace constants for any finite, exhaustive set; an `enum`-shaped type defined as a bag of `const` strings/ints is forbidden.
Type values are **immutable** — fields are read-only after construction (TS `readonly`, Go unexported + getter, PHP `readonly` properties); mutator methods on type structs are forbidden.
The cross-language SSOT for shared types is `03-common-type-definitions.md` and includes at minimum: `ContentType`, `HttpMethod`, `HttpStatus`, `SortDirection`, `Environment`.
Each common type has identical semantic values across Go/TS/PHP (e.g., `HttpMethod.Get` is the same string in all 3 languages); divergence is a doc/code bug.
`ContentType` and `HttpStatus` use the canonical IANA/HTTP names; project-specific aliases (e.g., `JsonResponse` for `application/json`) are forbidden in the shared type.
`SortDirection` is a 2-value enum (`Asc`/`Desc`) — string literal `"asc"`/`"desc"` in business logic is forbidden.
Anti-patterns listed in §04 (god-types files, circular type dependencies, runtime-only types in `types/`, `any`/`interface{}` in shared types) MUST NOT appear in the codebase.
The summary checklist in §04 maps 1:1 to `AT-TYPESFOLDERCONVENTION-01..12`; orphan checklist items fail review.

The convention is mirrored in language-specific specs (Go `02-coding-guidelines/03-golang/`, TS `02-coding-guidelines/02-typescript/`, PHP `02-coding-guidelines/04-php/`); divergence between this SSOT and a language spec is a doc bug.

The frontend stack MUST be Vite 5 + React 18 + TypeScript 5 + Tailwind v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite` in `src/index.css` `@theme` block); proposing Next.js, CRA, Vue, Svelte, or Tailwind v3 is forbidden because it contradicts the pinned-dependency matrix.
NO backend runtime (Node server, Go, PHP, Supabase, sql.js, IndexedDB) MAY be referenced in any architecture file — backend choice is DEFERRED per `mem://constraints/backend-runtime-deferred`.
Every dependency added to `package.json` MUST be justified in the tech-stack file with a one-line rationale; un-rationalised additions fail review.
Every route MUST be documented with: URL pattern, page-component name, focus-on-mount target, AND scroll-restoration policy; partial entries fail review.
Routes MUST use React Router v6 declarative `<Route>` config in `src/App.tsx`; file-based routing (Next-style) is forbidden because it contradicts the Vite + React Router stack decision.

The contract map MUST be auto-regenerated by `scripts/spec-hygiene/` on every CI run; manual edits to the auto-generated section between sentinels fail review.

All architecture decisions MUST be runtime-agnostic — no assumption about whether persistence is local, WordPress, or anything else; assumptions about backend leak through and fail review.
App uses React 18 + Vite 5 + TypeScript 5. No Next.js, Vue, Svelte, or Angular.

All interactive elements meet WCAG 2.1 AA: 4.5:1 text contrast, visible focus ring, full keyboard reachability.

Every async surface ships **all three** of: loading state, empty state, error state — no silent blank UI.

All colors MUST be HSL semantic tokens defined in `src/index.css` inside the `@theme` block; raw hex / RGB / OKLCH values in components or CSS files are FORBIDDEN as a Code-Red design-system bug.

Code blocks MUST use Geist Mono (or documented monospace fallback); UI text MUST use Inter (or documented system fallback). Other webfonts require a documented loading-budget rationale.

shadcn-ui components MUST be customised via the design system (variants/`cva`), NOT by editing the component's source unless via documented patch in `components/ui/`; un-tracked shadcn edits fail review.

Allowed inline formats MUST be limited to: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, link; arbitrary spans, font sizes, or colors in body content are FORBIDDEN.
Links MUST be normalized to absolute URLs at save time AND open with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; raw `javascript:` URLs MUST be rejected at parse boundary.
Pasted HTML MUST be sanitized through a documented allow-list parser; raw `innerHTML = pastedContent` is a Code-Red XSS bug.
Enter behavior MUST be specified for EVERY one of the 12 item types (per `mem://features/core-mechanics`); missing any type fails review.
`Enter` on a non-empty bullet MUST create a new sibling at the same indent; `Shift+Enter` MUST insert a soft line-break inside the current bullet.
`Enter` on an empty bullet at indent ≥ 1 MUST out-dent (NOT delete); on an empty bullet at indent 0 MUST be a no-op (NOT focus loss).
`Tab` MUST indent (only if a previous sibling exists); `Shift+Tab` MUST out-dent; both MUST preserve the cursor offset within the bullet text.
Drag-and-drop MUST distinguish three drop targets: before-sibling, after-sibling, child-of; ambiguous drops fail review. The drop indicator MUST show which target is active.
Default drag MUST move the node; `Alt`/`Option` modifier MUST create a mirror (NOT a deep copy); other modifiers MUST be no-ops (no surprise behavior).
Auto-scroll near viewport edges MUST kick in within 60 px of the edge with a documented velocity curve; fixed-velocity or no-auto-scroll fails review.
Dragging a node onto its own descendant MUST be rejected with a visible "not-allowed" cursor; silent rejection is a Code-Red UX bug.
All keyboard shortcuts in the editor MUST match `spec/31-app/01-features/05-interactions.md` byte-for-byte; divergence is a Code-Red consistency bug.
Multi-select MUST follow Shift-click (range) AND Cmd/Ctrl-click (additive) semantics per `mem://features/multi-select`; other semantics fail review.
Cursor position MUST be preserved across every undo/redo, indent/outdent, move, and mirror operation; cursor reset to position 0 on any of these is a Code-Red UX bug.
IME composition events (`compositionstart` / `compositionend`) MUST suppress autosave AND undo-stack pushes during composition; IME-mid-state autosaves are a Code-Red data-corruption bug.
Autosave MUST be debounced (≥ 500ms); per-keystroke saves are a Code-Red perf bug. Autosave MUST queue offline per `mem://features/offline-resilience`.
Undo/redo MUST be granular per logical operation (NOT per character); per-character undo is a Code-Red UX bug because users expect word-level grouping at minimum.
All theme/component combinations MUST meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text + UI elements); failing combinations are a Code-Red accessibility bug.
All interactive targets MUST be ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size Minimum); smaller targets are a Code-Red accessibility bug.
Every interactive element MUST have a visible focus ring with ≥ 3:1 contrast against its background; suppressing the focus ring (`outline: none` without replacement) is a Code-Red bug.
The full editor MUST be operable by keyboard alone (no mouse-only paths); any feature inaccessible by keyboard is a Code-Red accessibility bug.
All non-decorative images / icons MUST have `alt` text or `aria-label`; decorative SVGs MUST set `aria-hidden="true"`; missing either is a Code-Red bug.
Live regions (toasts, autosave indicators) MUST use `aria-live="polite"` (or `assertive` only for errors); missing live-region semantics is a Code-Red SR bug.
A 250-item viewport MUST render in < 16 ms (sustained 60 fps target); breaching is a Code-Red perf bug per `mem://architecture/data-model` 250-item cap.
Initial JS bundle (first load, gzipped) MUST be ≤ 250 KB; route-split chunks ≤ 100 KB; CI MUST fail on budget breach.
Lighthouse Performance score on the editor route MUST be ≥ 90 on a documented mid-tier mobile profile; < 90 fails review.
Lists with > 50 items MUST use virtualization (react-virtual or equivalent) OR a documented windowing strategy; un-virtualized > 50-item lists are a Code-Red perf bug.
Images MUST be lazy-loaded (`loading="lazy"`) below the fold; eager-loaded below-fold images are a perf bug.
EVERY async surface MUST specify all four states: idle, loading, empty, error; missing any of the four fails review because users see blank screens.
Loading states MUST appear within 100 ms of fetch start (or use optimistic UI); silent > 100ms gaps are a Code-Red UX bug.
Error states MUST offer a documented recovery action (retry / undo / contact); dead-end error screens are a Code-Red UX bug.
Empty states MUST include: an illustration/icon, a one-line explanation, AND a primary CTA (when an action is possible); 3-of-3-missing empty states fail review.

The global store MUST be Zustand with one slice per concern (selection, focus, drag, expansion, search); a single monolithic slice is forbidden because it forces every consumer to re-render on any change.
Component state MUST use `useState` / `useReducer` for local-only concerns; promoting local state to the global store without a documented cross-component need fails review.
Selectors MUST return primitives or stable references (use `shallow` equality for objects); selectors that build a new object on every call cause re-render storms and are a Code-Red perf bug.
Async actions MUST go through documented thunks/handlers (NOT inline `set` calls inside `await`); inline async-`set` is a Code-Red race-condition bug.
Data flow MUST be unidirectional: store → selector → component → action → store; two-way binding (component-mutates-prop-back-up) is FORBIDDEN as a Code-Red architecture bug.
Every action MUST be named verb-first (`addItem`, `moveNode`, NOT `itemAdded` / `nodeMover`); past-tense and noun-named actions fail review because they obscure intent.
NO backend runtime MAY be named in any data-flow file — the persistence layer is an injected `Persistence` interface, NOT a concrete backend; naming WordPress/Supabase/sql.js fails review.
Optimistic updates MUST include rollback on failure; one-way optimistic-only updates are a Code-Red data-integrity bug.
Every domain type MUST extend the unified `Item` interface (`id`, `parentId`, `content`, `itemType`); separate "Bullet" / "Todo" / "Heading" interfaces are FORBIDDEN — discriminate via `itemType`.
All type names, JSON keys, AND DB column names MUST be PascalCase singular; deviations fail review per cross-language naming SSOT.
Boundary parsing MUST use Zod schemas (`z.infer<typeof Schema>` as the type SSOT); hand-rolled type-guards in business code fail review.
Discriminated unions for `itemType` MUST have an `assertNever(x)` exhaustiveness default in every switch; missing default is a Code-Red maintainability bug.
The viewport MUST cap at 250 items per render (per data-model SSOT); breaking the cap is a Code-Red perf bug because it tanks 60fps target.
Item ordering MUST use fractional indexing (NOT integer position re-numbering on every move); integer-renumber-on-move is a Code-Red perf bug at 250 items.
Mirrored nodes MUST share the same source `Item` reference (NOT deep clones); deep-cloning mirrors is a Code-Red sync-divergence bug.
`User` table MUST be singular PascalCase with `UserId` PK as `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` (FR-1) — UUID PKs are forbidden because they prevent efficient joins on the per-user shard key.
Roles MUST live in a separate `UserRole` table linking `UserId` ↔ `Role` enum (FR-2); storing role columns directly on `User` is a Code-Red privilege-escalation bug per the project memory rule.
The `Role` enum MUST be exactly `User`, `Editor`, `Admin`; adding new roles MUST update the enum + capability matrix + this AT — magic-string roles are forbidden.
The capability matrix in `00-overview.md` MUST be the SSOT — code MUST NOT introduce ad-hoc capabilities not listed; new capabilities require updating the matrix first.
All RBAC checks MUST go through the central `hasRole(userId, role)` helper (FR-6) — inline role comparisons (`if (user.role === 'Admin')`) are forbidden because they're un-auditable.
`hasRole` MUST be the security-definer pattern: it MUST query the `UserRole` table (NOT a session cache) for privilege-elevation checks, even though session cache may be used for UI rendering.
Auth MUST support password + optional WebAuthn passkey (FR-3); password-only auth without a documented passkey upgrade path fails review.
Passwords MUST be hashed with Argon2id (memory ≥ 64 MB, iterations ≥ 3, parallelism ≥ 1) — bcrypt/PBKDF2/SHA-256 are forbidden as they're below the 2026 baseline.
Session tokens MUST live in `httpOnly` + `Secure` + `SameSite=Lax` cookies when sync is enabled (FR-4); `localStorage` fallback is allowed ONLY in solo (no-sync) mode.
JWTs (if used) MUST carry only the `userId` reference (NOT user data); embedding role/permissions in JWT claims is a Code-Red privilege-escalation bug.
Solo mode MUST work with NO server login required; forcing login for offline use is a Code-Red product-promise violation.
Switching from solo → sync mode MUST migrate the local user data into the synced account WITHOUT data loss; partial migration is a Code-Red data-loss bug.
Admin UI MUST support invite, deactivate, role-change (FR-5); deletion MUST be a separate flow gated by an additional confirmation (NOT folded into deactivate).
Every admin action MUST emit an entry to the activity feed (audit-of-the-audit); silent admin actions are a Code-Red audit-integrity bug.
Per-item sharing permissions MUST follow the sharing-model memory; admin override of share permissions MUST be logged AND user-notified — silent override is a Code-Red trust bug.

A user MUST be able to: (a) export all their data as a single archive, (b) delete their account in one operation that purges per-user DB + sessions + feedback + activity events. Piecemeal deletion fails GDPR.
Per-user data MUST live under `data/users/<userIdHash>/…` (hash, NOT raw ID) — using raw user IDs in directory paths is a Code-Red privacy bug.
The user-id hash MUST be deterministic (HMAC-SHA256 with a server-side secret) — using a non-keyed SHA-256 enables enumeration and is forbidden.
Directory traversal protection: any path computed from user input MUST go through `path.Clean` + prefix-check against the user's scope root; missing the prefix-check is a Code-Red OWASP bug.
Per-user DB files are SQLite, named `data/users/<userIdHash>/user.sqlite`; sharing a single SQLite file across users is forbidden.
All per-user tables include the user's `UserId` column anyway (defense in depth — even though they're physically isolated); missing the column fails review.
The `UserDbManager` is the SOLE source of per-user DB handles; bespoke `sql.Open(perUserPath)` calls outside the manager are forbidden.
The manager MUST cap per-user pool size (default 4 conns, configurable via seedable-config); unbounded pools are a Code-Red resource bug.
The manager MUST evict idle handles after a documented TTL (default 15 min); leaking handles across long sessions is a Code-Red resource bug.
Every example MUST resolve the user handle via `mgr.For(ctx, userId)` — passing a raw `*sql.DB` around is forbidden (loses isolation guarantees).
Cross-user reads (e.g., admin dashboards) MUST go through a documented `AdminAggregator` API that asserts the caller has the `Admin` role; raw cross-user iteration in business code is forbidden.
Sessions are server-side (NOT JWTs that hold user-data) — JWTs carry only the `userId` reference; embedding user data in JWT claims is a Code-Red privacy bug.
Session cookies are `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` (or stricter); missing any flag is a Code-Red OWASP bug.
Per-user data deletion MUST be a one-shot operation: `mgr.PurgeUser(userId)` removes the per-user directory + DB file + session entries + audit-log marker; partial deletion is a Code-Red GDPR bug.
Per-user data export MUST be a one-shot operation returning a single archive containing the user's DB + uploaded files + decrypted settings; piecemeal exports fail GDPR portability.

Hardcoded validation arrays in Go source files (e.g., `var allowedModels = []string{…}` with literal members) are FORBIDDEN — every such array MUST be sourced from `config.seed.json` via the `ValidationDataService`. Violations are a Code-Red configurability bug.

Each entry MUST carry `category`, `key`, `value`, and `version` fields; missing any field MUST fail seed-load with a typed error (NOT a panic).
Validation data MUST persist in the **Root DB** under a `validation_data` table with `(category, key)` as the composite primary key; per-user copies are forbidden (this data is global).

`ValidationDataService` MUST be the SOLE read path; bespoke `SELECT … FROM validation_data` queries in business code are forbidden.
The service MUST cache reads in-memory with a documented TTL (default 5 min) and MUST expose an `Invalidate(category)` hook so admin edits propagate within the next request.
Seed-version conflicts (DB version > seed version) MUST keep the DB row (user wins); version regressions MUST be logged at WARN level — silent overwrite is a Code-Red data-loss bug.
Each category MUST have a documented owner (team or individual) recorded in `06-categories-and-versioning.md`; orphan categories fail review.
The runtime API MUST expose `Get(category, key)` returning `(value, ok)` and `List(category)` returning `[]Entry`; mutation APIs (write/delete) MUST be admin-gated via the RBAC layer.
Every new validation feature MUST tick all 7 boxes of the per-feature checklist (define → seed → store → enum → service → validator → tests); merging without the checklist completed is forbidden.
The verbose-logging API exposes a single Logger interface with the documented level set (`Debug`, `Info`, `Warn`, `Error`); custom levels are forbidden.
Logger initialization happens **once** at process boot; subcommands receive an injected logger and MUST NOT call `NewLogger` themselves.
Log format is the documented structured form (key=value or JSON) with required fields `Ts`, `Level`, `Msg`, `Component`; ad-hoc `fmt.Println` for diagnostics is forbidden.
Each command follows the documented command-pattern wrapper that emits a `Started`/`Finished` pair with elapsed time at `Info` level (or `Debug` if `--quiet`).
Release-pipeline log points (`04-release-pipeline-log-points.md`) MUST appear in the order documented; missing a documented log point in a release run is a defect.
Logger constants (level names, env var names, default file paths) live in the constants reference and are not duplicated inline.
Verbose mode is opt-in via the global `--verbose` / `-v` flag and the `LOG_LEVEL` env var; default level is `Info`.
Logging MUST NOT log secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords); a secret-redaction step runs before any log line is emitted — Code Red on bypass.
Every screenshot in the gallery MUST exist in BOTH light and dark variants under `public/images/guide/`; missing either variant fails review.
All colors in rendered components MUST come from CSS custom properties (HSL); inline hex/rgb literals in component files are a Code-Red design-system bug.
Folder/tree blocks MUST be auto-detected from a fenced code block tagged `tree` OR `folder`; manual class-based opt-in is forbidden because authors will forget.
Code blocks MUST always render in a dark theme regardless of the app theme; switching code-block theme with the app theme is forbidden because it harms syntax-highlight contrast.
Each code block MUST display a language badge derived from the fence info-string (`” ```ts ”` → `TS`); missing badge fails review.
Heading animations MUST honour `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and disable transforms/opacity transitions; ignoring the media query is a Code-Red accessibility bug.
External links MUST render with an outbound icon AND `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; missing `rel` is a Code-Red security bug (tab-nabbing).
Tables MUST be horizontally scrollable on viewports < 768 px (NOT clipped, NOT wrapped); clipped tables fail review.
Checklists MUST render `- [ ]` / `- [x]` as semantic checkboxes (read-only in preview, interactive in edit mode); plain-text rendering fails review.
TOC MUST use `IntersectionObserver` (NOT scroll-event throttling) to highlight the active heading; scroll-event polling is forbidden because of perf cost.
TOC MUST be sticky on viewports ≥ 1024 px and collapse to a top-bar dropdown below that breakpoint.
Animation timing MUST come from a shared timing-tokens module (`--motion-fast: 120ms`, etc.); inline `transition: 230ms` literals fail review.
View modes MUST be one of `preview / edit / split`; adding a new mode requires updating the typed enum + this AT — string-only modes are forbidden.
Split-view editor MUST sync scroll position between panes within 16 ms (one frame); scroll desync > 1 frame fails review.
Welcome/landing page MUST be reachable via a deep-link (`/welcome`) AND MUST be the default view when no document is open; missing either path fails review.
Sidebar tree MUST persist expand/collapse state per-user across reloads (via `localStorage` keyed by user-id-hash); resetting state on reload fails review.
Sidebar search MUST filter as-you-type with ≤ 100 ms keystroke→render latency on a 1k-node tree; slower filtering fails the perf budget.
Every new visual feature MUST tick all checklist items in `13-checklist-and-references.md` (component, story, screenshot light, screenshot dark, AT updated); merging without all five fails review.
Every row MUST render exactly 5 anatomy slots in fixed order: ⋯ (drag/menu) · ▸/▾ (expand) · ● (bullet dot) · content · + (add child); reordering or omitting slots is a Code-Red layout bug.
Hover state MUST reveal ⋯ AND + within 50 ms; longer reveal latency or missing affordances is a UX bug because it breaks discoverability.
The expand arrow ▸ MUST rotate 90° to ▾ on expansion via CSS transform (NOT swapping two glyphs); glyph-swap is forbidden because it skips animation.

Clicking the bullet dot ● MUST zoom into the node (push focus + URL); ⌘/Ctrl-click on the dot MUST toggle multi-select WITHOUT zooming. Same-binding-different-modifier is required (per `mem://features/multi-select`).
An empty-content row MUST still render the dot AND expand caret AND remain selectable; collapsing empty rows is FORBIDDEN because it breaks placeholder UX.
Every interactive target in the row MUST be ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px hit area (per WCAG 2.5.8); smaller targets are a Code-Red accessibility bug.
Right-click on a row OR clicking ⋯ MUST open the per-row context menu at the cursor position (NOT a fixed location); fixed-position menu is a UX bug.
The per-row menu MUST close on outside click, `Esc`, OR action completion; menus that persist after action fire are a Code-Red UX bug.
Menu item order MUST be locked (per visual reference); reordering between releases is FORBIDDEN because it breaks muscle memory.
The focused-item ⋯ menu MUST present a DIFFERENT action set than the per-row ⋯ menu (e.g. share, export, delete-current-focus); identical action sets are a Code-Red spec bug.
The focused-item menu MUST be reachable via keyboard (`Shift+F10` or documented equivalent); mouse-only menus are a Code-Red accessibility bug.
The comment icon MUST appear ONLY when the row has ≥ 1 comment OR is being hovered; always-visible comment icons are a UX bug because they add visual noise.
Clicking the comment icon MUST open a thread panel as a right-side overlay (distinct from the Phase 3 right-side details panel); collapsing the two panels into one is FORBIDDEN.
Unread comments MUST show a numeric badge with `aria-label="N unread comments"`; missing aria-label is a Code-Red SR bug.
Bullet dot color states (default / focused / multi-selected / mirrored) MUST come from semantic HSL tokens (per `03-design-system` AT-UIDS-01); hardcoded colors fail review.

The `/today` route MUST render all items where `date = today` OR `starred = true`; deviating from the union semantics is a Code-Red spec bug.

Today items MUST be sortable by exactly three modes: manual order (default), time-of-day, alpha; additional sort modes require a separate spec amendment.
The selected sort mode MUST persist across reloads via local preferences (per `08-app-shell` AT-WFSHELL-13).
An empty Today view MUST render the empty-state contract (illustration + one-line + CTA per `05-quality` AT-UIQA-15); blank screens are a Code-Red UX bug.
`⌘⇧N` (Mac) / `Ctrl+Shift+N` (Win/Linux) MUST open the Quick Add modal from ANY context, including inside the editor; suppression in editors is a Code-Red UX bug.
The modal MUST close on `Esc` (cancel), `Enter` (submit), OR click-outside (cancel); missing any path is a Code-Red UX bug.
Submission MUST append a new node to Inbox AND show a confirmation toast within 100 ms; silent submission is a UX bug.
The modal MUST trap focus AND auto-focus the input on open; missing auto-focus is a Code-Red accessibility bug.

Clicking a date in the calendar MUST open the date-filter search results AND update the URL (deep-linkable); missing URL update is a Code-Red routing bug.
Calendar week-start (Sunday vs Monday) MUST follow the user's locale OR a documented Settings toggle; hardcoded week-start is a localization bug.
The slash menu MUST open on `/` keypress at start-of-line OR after whitespace (NOT mid-word); mid-word `/` MUST insert a literal slash.
The menu order MUST match the documented visual reference (img-53) byte-for-byte; reordering items between releases is FORBIDDEN.
